text: But the workers' compensation insurer may not indemnify the employer against this penalty (see ¶ 3:549). [3:528 - 3:534] Reserved. 3. [3:535] Coverage for Injuries Caused by Employment Termination: Injuries resulting from nonconsensual termination of employment are included within the scope of workers' compensation as “both the act of termination and the acts leading up to termination necessarily arise out of and occur during and in the course of the employment.” [Shoemaker v. Myers (1990) 52 C3d 1, 19-20, 276 CR 303, 314; see Wong v. State Comp. Ins. Fund (1993) 12 CA4th 686, 694, 16 CR2d 1, 5 (disapproved on other grounds by La Jolla Beach & Tennis Club, Inc. v. Industrial Indem. Co. (1994) 9 C4th 27, 36 CR2d 100)—constructive discharge] “If the actions of the employer in terminating the employee ‘constitute a normal part of the employment relationship,’ injuries which result are subject to the exclusive remedy provisions of Labor Code section 3602.” [B & E Convalescent Ctr. v. State Comp. Ins. Fund (1992) 8 CA4th 78, 89, 9 CR2d 894, 901] a.
